scope: Controlled external authority and peer-reviewed source registry for THC-ENC claim-level evidence collection. Source inclusion does not approve a lesson, publish a draft, or complete independent science review.
rules: Source records identify authority and applicability; they do not create publication authorization.
Every lesson-level claim mapping must remain review-pending until independently reviewed.
Regulatory and standards sources must be rechecked at release time because requirements can change.
Project-internal source packets may guide architecture, but external source records are preferred for claim-level evidence.

sources.title: NIH Grants & Funding: Enhancing Reproducibility through Rigor and Transparency
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for general evidence-discipline, reproducibility, rigor, and transparent-reporting expectations. It is not cannabis-specific and does not rank individual cultivation claims.

sources.title: Papoutsoglou et al. (2020). Enabling reusability of plant phenomic datasets with MIAPPE 1.1.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for plant-phenotyping metadata, protocol, environmental-context, and reusable dataset requirements. It is a plant phenomics standard, not a cannabis cultivation recipe.

sources.title: Livingston et al. (2023). Glandular trichome development, morphology, and maturation are influenced by plant age and genotype in high THC-containing cannabis.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for cannabis-specific trichome-development and maturation evidence. Apply within the studied genotype, tissue, age, and method boundaries.

sources.title: Postharvest Operations of Cannabis and Their Effect on Cannabinoid Content: A Review.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for drying, trimming, equilibrium moisture, sorption, curing, storage, packaging, and cannabinoid-context overview. Review-level evidence must be mapped to specific claims and not treated as universal target proof.

sources.title: Post-Harvest Operations to Generate High-Quality Medicinal Cannabis Products: A Systematic Review.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for medicinal-cannabis postharvest quality factors, moisture, light, temperature, duration, and drying-technique context. It does not establish one universal postharvest protocol.

sources.title: The influence of drying and storage conditions on the volatilome and cannabinoid content of Cannabis sativa L. inflorescences.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for controlled drying/storage comparisons and measured volatile/cannabinoid outcomes. Apply only within the tested varieties, storage conditions, and analytical methods.

sources.title: NIST: Metrological Traceability Frequently Asked Questions and NIST Policy.
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for traceability, calibration records, measurement uncertainty, measurand clarity, and fitness-for-purpose boundaries. It is not cannabis-specific and does not validate a particular device.

sources.title: NOAA NCEI: U.S. Climate Normals, 1991-2020.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for U.S. station climate-normal baselines. Normals describe historical distributions and are not crop forecasts or site-specific risk guarantees.

sources.title: USDA NRCS: Web Soil Survey.
sources.publisher: United States Department of Agriculture Natural Resources Conservation Service
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for mapped U.S. soil-resource planning information. Onsite sampling, current field conditions, drainage, contamination, and engineering constraints still require verification.

sources.title: USDA NRCS: Conservation Practice Standards.
sources.publisher: United States Department of Agriculture Natural Resources Conservation Service
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for minimum science-based conservation-practice criteria and as an index to practice-specific standards. Local Field Office Technical Guide, engineering review, law, and site conditions control implementation.

sources.title: USDA NRCS: Irrigation Water Management Conservation Practice Standard 449.
sources.publisher: United States Department of Agriculture Natural Resources Conservation Service
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for irrigation-water-management planning criteria. It is not a cannabis-specific irrigation schedule and requires local technical review.

sources.title: USDA NRCS: Irrigation System, Microirrigation Conservation Practice Standard 441.
sources.publisher: United States Department of Agriculture Natural Resources Conservation Service
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for microirrigation planning/design criteria. It does not replace local design, water-quality review, pressure testing, or crop-specific validation.

sources.title: Loreti and Perata (2020). The Many Facets of Hypoxia in Plants.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for plant oxygen sensing, hypoxia physiology, respiration constraints, waterlogging context, and plant responses to low oxygen. It is general plant physiology rather than cannabis-specific production evidence.

sources.title: Zarebanadkouki et al. (2019). Root water uptake and its pathways across the root: quantification at the cellular scale.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for apoplastic and cell-to-cell root-water transport pathways and method-aware root hydraulics. The experiment used lupin, so mechanism can inform cannabis physiology but species-specific quantitative transfer is not justified.

sources.title: Blatt (2024). A charged existence: A century of transmembrane ion transport in plants.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for plant membrane ion transport, electrochemical gradients, transport proteins, and energy coupling. It is broad plant physiology and does not establish cannabis-specific nutrient targets or transporter kinetics.

sources.title: Cockson et al. (2019). Characterization of Nutrient Disorders of Cannabis sativa.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for cannabis-specific nutrient omission/toxicity symptom characterization, MRML tissue-analysis context, and staged visual symptom documentation. Do not treat one cultivar and sand-culture protocol as universal field or production diagnostic proof.

sources.title: Saloner and Bernstein (2020). Response of Medical Cannabis (Cannabis sativa L.) to Nitrogen Supply Under Long Photoperiod.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for controlled cannabis nitrogen-response evidence under long photoperiod, including biomass, photosynthesis, water relations, and ionome changes across N supply levels. Do not convert the tested mg/L levels into universal cultivar, substrate, or lifecycle prescriptions.

sources.title: Grassa et al. (2021). A new Cannabis genome assembly associates elevated cannabidiol (CBD) with hemp introgressed into marijuana.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for chromosome-resolved cannabis genome assembly, cannabinoid synthase locus architecture, CBDAS introgression, and the limit that synthase loci do not fully explain overall potency. Do not use as proof that a detected marker predicts complete crop performance.

sources.title: Punja et al. (2025). Transmission, Spread, Longevity and Management of Hop Latent Viroid, a Widespread and Destructive Pathogen Affecting Cannabis (Cannabis sativa L.) Plants in North America.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for HLVd transmission, spread, persistence, detection, sanitation-treatment, and meristem-culture management evidence in cannabis systems. Maintain assay, genotype, tissue, timing, and management-context limits; visual symptoms alone are not diagnostic.

sources.title: Wu et al. (2019). An Update on Plant Photobiology and Implications for Cannabis Production.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for cannabis-production photobiology framing, including wavelength, intensity, photoperiod, photoreceptors, photosynthesis, photomorphogenesis, and lighting-system implications. It is a review and should not be treated as a cultivar-specific light recipe.

sources.title: Danziger and Bernstein (2021). Light matters: Effect of light spectra on cannabinoid profile and plant development of medical cannabis (Cannabis sativa L.).
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for cannabis-specific evidence that light spectrum can affect inflorescence yield, morphology, and cannabinoid profile in cultivar-dependent ways. Do not generalize one spectrum, cultivar set, or fixture context into a universal production prescription.

sources.title: Hahm et al. (2025). High light intensity enhances cannabinoid biosynthesis through concerted gene expression in hemp (Cannabis sativa) flowers.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for controlled hemp flowering evidence comparing 200, 400, and 600 micromol m-2 s-1 white LED intensity and measured biomass, cannabinoids, and biosynthesis-gene expression. Do not treat 600 micromol m-2 s-1 as a universal optimum for all cultivars, rooms, spectra, CO2, economics, or legal product goals.

sources.title: Backer et al. (2019). Closing the Yield Gap for Cannabis: A Meta-Analysis of Factors Determining Cannabis Yield.
sources.useAndLimitations: Use for evidence that cannabis yield is influenced by interacting factors including variety, density, light intensity, light type, photoperiod or flowering duration, fertilization, and container variables. Meta-analysis supports multifactor framing, not a single-light-factor release claim.
